title: Ray‑Ban Heir Reveals Shocking Pregnancy Mystery with Ex Jessica Serfaty: “It Could Be You or Him”
body:
A former billionaire heir to the iconic Ray‑Ban eyewear empire has opened up about a baffling pregnancy saga that unfolded last summer with his ex‑fiancée, former soap‑opera star Jessica Serfaty, while also confronting fresh legal accusations that she allegedly supplied a teenager with ketamine at a Los Angeles birthday celebration. The revelations, disclosed in a recent court filing and a candid interview, have thrust both parties into a media frenzy that blends celebrity intrigue, high‑stakes romance, and a looming criminal investigation.

Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio, the Italian‑American businessman who inherited a multibillion‑dollar stake in Luxottica, confirmed that Serfaty told him she was expecting a child during a heated exchange in July. “I was pregnant – it could be you or him,” she reportedly said, leaving Del Vecchio to wonder whether the father was himself or another man she had been seeing. The ambiguous declaration, made just weeks before their highly publicized engagement was called off, has since become a focal point of gossip columns and legal documents alike. While Del Vecchio has not publicly commented on the paternity question, his legal team filed a motion seeking clarification, citing concerns over potential financial obligations and the impact on his family’s reputation.

The drama deepened when a Los Angeles County court record surfaced, alleging that Serfary, now 31, provided a 16‑year‑old guest at her birthday party with a dose of ketamine—a powerful dissociative anesthetic often misused as a recreational drug. Prosecutors say the teenager was given the substance without parental consent, prompting an investigation into possible child endangerment charges. Serfary’s representatives have denied the allegations, labeling the filing as “baseless” and insisting that the party was a “private family gathering” where no illicit substances were present. Nonetheless, the claim has reignited public scrutiny of Serfary’s past behavior, which includes a string of high‑profile relationships and a brief stint as a model for luxury brands.

Industry analysts note that the entanglement of personal scandal with legal jeopardy can have tangible repercussions for both individuals’ professional prospects. For Del Vecchio, whose family’s holdings include the world’s largest eyewear conglomerate, any perception of impropriety could affect shareholder confidence and the brand’s market positioning, especially as Luxottica navigates a competitive landscape marked by shifting consumer preferences and sustainability pressures. Meanwhile, Serfary’s career, already marked by intermittent acting roles and modeling gigs, may suffer further setbacks if the ketamine allegations lead to criminal proceedings or civil liability, potentially limiting future endorsements and casting calls.

Legal experts point out that the paternity issue, though sensational, is largely a civil matter that could be resolved through DNA testing, should either party pursue it. However, the timing of the alleged pregnancy—coinciding with the breakup—adds complexity to any potential settlement, as child support obligations and asset division would need to be negotiated amid ongoing litigation. In parallel, the ketamine case raises questions about the responsibilities of hosts in private events, especially when minors are present. California law imposes strict penalties for providing controlled substances to underage individuals, and prosecutors are expected to evaluate whether Serfary’s actions constitute criminal negligence or a more serious felony.

As the legal processes unfold, both Del Vecchio and Serfary appear to be navigating parallel battles: one over personal legacy and financial responsibility, the other over criminal accountability. Observers suggest that the outcomes could set precedents for how high‑net‑worth individuals manage private indiscretions that become public. For now, the spotlight remains firmly on the two former lovers, whose intertwined narratives of love, uncertainty, and alleged wrongdoing continue to capture the public’s imagination.

Looking ahead, the courts will likely determine whether a paternity test will be ordered and whether the ketamine allegations will proceed to trial. Both scenarios could have lasting implications—not only for the individuals involved but also for the broader conversation about celebrity privacy, legal accountability, and the responsibilities that accompany wealth and fame. The coming weeks promise further developments that will shape the reputations and futures of those at the center of this extraordinary saga.
